Chapter 3 ended with the spirit God gave (3:24). This chapter first tests the spirits (verses 1-6), then turns to love, named in every verse from 7 to 12 and from 16 to 21. Twice it says "God is love" (verses 8, 16), the only places in Scripture that do.

The false prophets "have gone out," the verb of 2:19: there "from us," here "into the world" (verse 1). As it stands, the confession of verse 2 is that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; read the other way, that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh. Verses 4, 5 and 6 open with "You yourselves," "They themselves," "We ourselves," each "from" God or the world. Read "error," the second spirit is named by what is false; read "leading astray," by what it does, as in 2:26. Deuteronomy 13:1-3. A sign that comes about does not decide it; where the prophet leads does. Yahweh's test is "whether you love." John 8:47. Here the one from God hears "the words of God," and those "not from God" do not hear. Verse 6: "whoever is not from God does not hear us."

"From God" comes eight times in verses 1-7, then not again. Spirits were tested for it (verse 1); now "love is from God" (verse 7). Verse 11 does not say we ought to love God in return, but "one another." Verse 12 sets two sentences side by side with nothing joining them: no one has ever gazed at God; if we love one another, God remains in us. John 1:18 has the same three Greek words, "God," "no one," "ever," with "seen" for "gazed." In Exodus 24:9-11 the leaders of Israel see the God of Israel. John 3:16-17. Verse 9 has their words, "only Son," "into the world," "through him." And "God loved ... in this way" is said of "the world" there, of "us" in verse 11. Deuteronomy 7:7-8. Not Israel's numbers, but Yahweh's love and his oath. Verse 10 has the same "not" and "but": "not that we ourselves have loved God, but that he himself loved us."

"Remain" comes six times in verses 12-16, three times both ways (verses 13, 15, 16). Three things go with it: the spirit he has given, confessing that Jesus is the Son of God, and remaining in love. The first two were the matter of verses 1-6; love, of verses 7-12. Verse 14 is the third time the chapter says the Son was sent: "so that we might live through him" (verse 9), "as the atonement" (verse 10), "as savior of the world." What is confessed in verse 15 is a statement; what is known and believed in verse 16 is "the love." Read "in us," God's love is within them; read "for us," it is toward them. John 4:42. "Savior of the world" is found in the New Testament only there and in verse 14, both times said by a "we ourselves" who heard or gazed.

"Made complete" comes four times in the letter: three times of love (2:5; 4:12, 17), and in verse 18 of a person, "the one who fears." "Fear" comes four times in verse 18 and nowhere else in the letter. In 3:3 and 3:7, "just as that one is" goes on to say what he is, "pure," "righteous"; verse 17 does not say. Verse 19 has the pair of verse 10, "we ourselves" and "he himself," and adds "first." As it stands it names no one we love; read "let us love," it is a call, as in verse 7; other copies add "him." Verse 20 comes back to verse 12: God unseen, and the brother seen. Zephaniah 3:15-17. On "that day" Zion is told "Do not fear," with Yahweh "in your midst," silent "in his love." Verses 17-18 have "the day of judgment" and love that "throws fear out." Mark 12:29-31. Jesus names a first commandment and a second. Verse 21 speaks of one, "this commandment," joining love of God and of the brother.
